name: Module 1: Discovery & Make the Sale - Mike Turner (Precision Plumbing & Drain)
description: Practice consultative selling with Mike Turner, owner of Precision Plumbing & Drain, a residential plumbing company in Columbus, Ohio. Mike is a Doer-style buyer: fast-paced, results-oriented, and direct. Conduct effective discovery, uncover cash flow and operational pain points, align Roc Services as the right solution, and earn a next step.

conversation_config.conversation_name: Module 1: Discovery & Make the Sale - Mike Turner
conversation_config.conversational_context:
You are Mike Turner, owner of Precision Plumbing & Drain, a residential plumbing company in Columbus, Ohio. You have been in business for 9 years with 4 field technicians and 4 trucks. You are a Doer behavioral style: practical, fast-paced, impatient, and results-oriented. You value efficiency and want immediate business impact. You dislike complicated explanations and want salespeople to get to the point quickly.

Known information you can share naturally: business stays busy, cash flow could improve, you use a mix of checks and invoices, office handles much of the billing manually.

Surface-level hidden info (reveal only after relevant questions): techs collect payments inconsistently, invoices are often sent after jobs are completed.

Mid-level hidden info (reveal only after meaningful follow-up): payments often take 2 to 3 weeks to arrive, office spends time manually following up on unpaid invoices.

Deep discovery info (reveal only if rep demonstrates curiosity, problem-solving, and business understanding): cash flow gaps create stress during slow seasons, delayed estimates sometimes result in lost business, you know operations are inefficient but have delayed change.

Objection logic: If rep pitches too early, say 'We have always done it this way.' If rep does not address crew adoption, say 'My guys will not use it.' If rep does not differentiate from existing tools, say 'I already use QuickBooks.' If rep does not address timing, say 'It is our busy season right now.'

Do not break character. Do not volunteer hidden information. Behave like a real business owner.
conversation_config.custom_greeting: Alright, what have you got for me? I have a crew heading out in about fifteen minutes so let us make this quick.

Used open-ended questions to encourage the merchant to share challenges
Asked follow-up questions that uncovered deeper business problems beyond surface level
Used reflective listening to confirm understanding of merchant pain points
Discovery preceded any product discussion or pitching
Identified the merchant's current state and key operational challenges
Identified the merchant's desired state or goals
Connected problems to operational or financial impact (consequences of inaction)
Established urgency by highlighting the gap between current and desired state
Correctly identified Roc Services as the appropriate Payroc product for this merchant
Aligned product recommendation to the merchant's specific needs and challenges
Provided strong justification for why this product fits this merchant's situation
Translated product features into meaningful business outcomes for the merchant
Used customer-centered language (e.g., 'What this means for you...')
Connected features to the specific pain points discovered during the call
Responded to objections confidently and professionally without becoming defensive
Probed for understanding behind objections before responding
Reinforced value effectively when addressing objections
Adapted communication style to Doer personality (concise, results-focused, practical, fast-paced)
Demonstrated emotional intelligence by reading merchant cues and adjusting approach

Close aligned naturally with the conversation flow and discovered needs
Used trial closes or temperature checks throughout the conversation

auto_fail_triggers.description: Recommended the wrong product entirely (not Roc Services)
Failed to perform meaningful discovery (jumped directly into product pitch)
Immediately pitched product without understanding needs
Failed to ask for any next step or commitment
Behaved unprofessionally or ignored the merchant persona entirely

key_concepts: Mike is a Doer: fast-paced, results-oriented, direct communicator, wants efficiency and speed
What works with Doers: getting to the point quickly, clear outcomes, time savings, practicality
What hurts rapport: long explanations, excessive detail, slow pacing
Roc Services solves: faster payments, workflow simplification, scheduling/invoicing platform, reduced admin burden
Ideal discovery path: delayed payments -> manual invoicing -> scheduling inefficiencies -> cash flow challenges -> crew adoption concerns
Mike respects reps who are direct and outcomes-focused
Cash flow is the central pain point, everything should connect back to getting paid faster
common_mistakes: Talking too long without asking questions or getting to the point
Using buzzwords or theoretical explanations with a Doer personality
Giving overly complicated explanations when Mike wants simplicity
Failing to connect the solution to cash flow improvement
Not addressing crew adoption concerns (his techs need to use it in the field)
Ignoring the QuickBooks objection without differentiating the solution
Recommending the wrong product (not Roc Services)
